en.title: What can aggregate randomized data establish about treatment duration and benefit–risk?
en.summary: SCOT trial efficacy and neuropathy compared with endpoint-specific denominators, uncertainty, missingness bounds and limits of joint benefit–risk inference.
key_findings: From published SCOT results, 3 vs 6 months of adjuvant chemotherapy changed 3-year DFS by −0.4 points (−2.6 to +1.8), while grade ≥2 neuropathy fell by 33.4 points (26.9 to 39.5).
Bounds that assign every missing neuropathy grade adversely still give a 27.6–36.6-point reduction within the safety cohort, so the toxicity benefit is robust to missing grades.
Efficacy and toxicity come from different populations, so a joint 'disease-free without neuropathy' probability is not identified; non-inferiority is not the same as identical efficacy.
en.seo_title: What can aggregate data show about treatment duration?
